title: Monitoring in living bacterial cells by UV-Vis spectroscopy
author: Tjusls China
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7y8hpzw

steps.title: Prepare culture with antibiotic and IPTG
steps.instruction: Pipette 5 µL of NDM‑28a BL21(DE3) glycerol stock into 5 mL LB medium, add 2.5 µL kanamycin, incubate at 37 °C with shaking until OD₆₀₀ reaches 0.5–0.6, then add IPTG to induce expression.

steps.title: Harvest and wash cells with phosphate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the culture to pellet the cells, resuspend the pellet in phosphate buffer, centrifuge again and discard the supernatant; repeat the resuspend‑centrifuge‑discard cycle three times to wash the cells.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge culture to collect pellet.
Resuspend pellet in phosphate buffer.
Centrifuge and discard supernatant.
Repeat resuspension and centrifugation two more times (total three washes).

steps.title: Resuspend and dilute to OD0.15
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed bacterial pellet in phosphate buffer, incubate as needed, and dilute the suspension so that the final OD₆₀₀ of the bacterial liquid used for measurements is 0.15.

steps.title: UV‑Vis Test I time course
steps.instruction: Set up four 100 µL reaction mixtures (each 95 µL bacterial liquid or buffer + 5 µL cefazolin, final cefazolin concentration 250 µM): (1) target‑protein‑expressing cells, (2) purified beta‑lactamase + cefazolin, (3) blank‑vector cells + cefazolin, (4) phosphate buffer + cefazolin. Record absorbance every 300 s for 12 readings, then plot absorbance versus time.

substeps.instruction: Prepare mixture A: 95 µL target‑protein‑expressing cells + 5 µL 250 µM cefazolin.
Prepare mixture B: 95 µL beta‑lactamase solution + 5 µL 250 µM cefazolin.
Prepare mixture C: 95 µL blank‑vector cells + 5 µL 250 µM cefazolin.
Prepare mixture D: 95 µL phosphate buffer + 5 µL 250 µM cefazolin.
Measure absorbance at the appropriate wavelength every 300 s for a total of 12 measurements.
Plot the time‑course UV‑Vis spectra.

steps.title: Determine optimal induction conditions
steps.instruction: For each sample of bacterial liquid harvested at different induction times or OD values, mix 95 µL of the sample with 5 µL cefazolin (250 µM). Record absorbance every 300 s for 24 readings to identify the induction time and OD giving the strongest signal.

substeps.instruction: Combine 95 µL bacterial sample (various induction times/ODs) with 5 µL 250 µM cefazolin.
Measure absorbance every 300 s for 24 time points.
Analyze the data to select the optimal induction time and cell density.

steps.title: UV‑Vis Test II antibiotic spectra
steps.instruction: Prepare four separate 100 µL mixtures (95 µL target‑protein‑expressing cells + 5 µL antibiotic, final antibiotic concentration 250 µM): cefazolin (measure at 273 nm), meropenem (307 nm), faropenem (300 nm), tetracycline (360 nm). Record the absorbance at the specified wavelength for each mixture.

substeps.instruction: Mix 95 µL target‑protein cells with 5 µL 250 µM cefazolin; measure at 273 nm.
Mix 95 µL target‑protein cells with 5 µL 250 µM meropenem; measure at 307 nm.
Mix 95 µL target‑protein cells with 5 µL 250 µM faropenem; measure at 300 nm.
Mix 95 µL target‑protein cells with 5 µL 250 µM tetracycline; measure at 360 nm.

steps.title: UV‑Vis Test III inhibition assay
steps.instruction: Set up inhibition reactions using 94 µL bacterial liquid (or phosphate buffer) + 5 µL cefazolin (250 µM) + 1 µL inhibitor or its 100 % DMSO solvent. Test a gradient of inhibitor concentrations with five parallel replicates per concentration. Record absorbance, calculate inhibition rate using Equation 1, and plot the IC₅₀ curve.

substeps.instruction: Prepare reaction A: 94 µL target‑protein cells + 5 µL 250 µM cefazolin + 1 µL inhibitor.
Prepare reaction B: 94 µL target‑protein cells + 5 µL 250 µM cefazolin + 1 µL inhibitor solvent (100 % DMSO).
Prepare reaction C: 94 µL phosphate buffer + 5 µL 250 µM cefazolin + 1 µL inhibitor solvent (100 % DMSO).
Prepare reaction D: 94 µL phosphate buffer + 5 µL cefazolin solvent + 1 µL inhibitor solvent (100 % DMSO).
Create a series of inhibitor concentrations (gradient) and include five parallel controls for each concentration.
Measure absorbance for each reaction.
Calculate inhibition rate% = 100 × [1 – ([St] – [Si])/([St] – [So])], where [St] = initial absorbance of antibiotic alone, [Si] = absorbance with inhibitor, [So] = absorbance with solvent only.
Plot inhibition rate versus inhibitor concentration to obtain the IC₅₀ curve.
